title: Esophageal manometry
what: A thin tube with sensors is passed through your nose into your food pipe. You take sips of water, and the device measures how the food pipe muscles work.
why: For trouble swallowing, chest pain with no clear cause, before reflux surgery, or before pH monitoring.
duration: usually 20 to 30 minutes; the report usually takes a few days
tell_doctor: All your medicines. Some affect the food pipe. Your doctor will say what to do with them
Surgery on your food pipe or stomach
Nose problems, such as a bent septum

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food or drink for 6 hours. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Ask your doctor in advance which ones to skip.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes with no tight collar.

steps: Your nose is numbed with a gel
A thin tube is passed through your nose while you swallow
You lie or sit and breathe calmly
On command, you take small sips of water, usually about ten
During the recording, do not talk or swallow extra
The tube is removed in a few seconds
feel: Putting in the tube is unpleasant: your eyes water, and you may gag
The sips feel odd, but do not hurt
after: You can eat and drink right away
Your nose may feel a little sore
The report usually takes a few days
red_flags: A nosebleed that will not stop, or severe chest pain: call emergency services

faq.q: Is it like an upper endoscopy?
faq.a: No. The tube is thinner, goes in through the nose, and shows nothing on a screen. It only measures pressure.

faq.q: Why is it done before pH monitoring?
faq.a: Manometry helps find the exact spot to place the pH sensor.

reminders.text: Esophageal manometry tomorrow. Do not eat or drink for the time the clinic told you. Bring a list of your medicines.
